knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Entry needs written authority from the responsible party and the controlling authority. A key and a neighbour's word do not provide it.
An entry log is the control record. The other two options are not entry controls and may breach privacy.

practicalCriteria: From a fictional case, the learner lists every party with an interest and identifies which written authority is missing. Pass: each interested party is named and the missing authority is identified.
The learner drafts an entry log with at least five required fields. Pass: the log includes person, purpose, time in, time out and the authority reference.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed entry-authorisation checklist for a fictional site
Blank entry log with required fields
stopWorkCriteria: A party offers access that the controlling authority has not confirmed.
